_doc: Clubs and part-time jobs (docs/GDD.md 4.13, Toru autoload). One club at a time (join at the club's place or the recruitment board, school 1F). A club meets on its `days` between `open` and `close` minutes; a session = pick a style, the clock jumps to `close`, `stat` (+ `also`) grows by base x style x skill bonus x goal gain. Every 4th session is the next `events` entry instead (own choices, fx = Town fx + stats/money). Jobs: interview once (`needs`: min_stat / no_flag / met), then work any `shifts` window {days, from, to} at the job's place; pay = per_hour x hours x bonus (game units, 1 = 100 yen), stats per shift. `where`: {level: suzunari|school, floor, tile}. `members` = who gets closer when you practise. Amane lines: `amane` (said when you join), `amane_day` (sometimes after a session).

styles.say: You push until your legs shake. Somebody notices; somebody always notices.
You do the work and laugh at the jokes. People sit a little closer to you afterwards.
You find the corner nobody looks at. Two hours pass. Nobody calls your name. That was the point.

job_styles.say: You never stop moving. The boss says nothing, which here means a lot.
You learn three names, two dogs' names and one secret recipe.
The hands of the clock move. Eventually.

board.name: Club recruitment board
board.text: Flyers on top of flyers. KENDO NEEDS BODIES. TRACK: RUN WITH INUKAI! THE OCCULT CLUB IS NOT A CULT (1 member). At the bottom, in tiny letters: GO-HOME CLUB - no meetings, no dues, no questions.
board.current: Your name is already on the {club} sheet.

kendo.name: Kendo Club
kendo.pitch: Gotoda-senpai, third year, built like a vending machine, blocks the budokan door. "Kendo is not about hitting people. It is about hitting people CORRECTLY. Mon, Wed, Fri. You'll get braver or you'll get bruised."
kendo.amane: "Kendo...? Senpai in armour... I'll bring towels. I'll bring all the towels."
kendo.amane_day: Amane waits outside the budokan with a towel folded into the shape of a cat.
sessions: Suburi: five hundred overhead cuts. Gotoda-senpai counts in a voice that rattles the shoji.
Footwork drills on the old floorboards. Every board squeaks a different note; the first-years swear one of them hums back.
Kakari-geiko: attack, attack, attack, until you forget to be scared of the man in front of you.

events.title: First practice match
events.text: Gotoda-senpai hands you a shinai. "One point. Against me. Don't hold back - I won't."

choices.say: You're on the floor in two seconds. Gotoda-senpai helps you up, grinning. "GOOD. Stupid, but brave."
You wait. And wait. When he finally moves, you move faster. A point, just. The whole club goes silent.
"...Next time," he says, not unkindly. You sit at the wall and watch for the rest of the hour.

events.title: The prefectural qualifier
events.text: A gym in the next town. Lacquered armour, shouting, the smell of other schools. Your bout is next.

choices.say: Men! The flag goes up on your side. Gotoda-senpai lifts you off the ground. Suzunari Gakuen makes the regional round for the first time in nine years.
You lose on points, but every point was yours. On the bus home nobody talks, and it feels like a good silence.

events.title: Somebody else's armour
events.text: Cleaning the storeroom you find a set of armour with a name tag stitched inside: ASAGIRI G. 1962.

choices.say: "That's the founder's. Some old guy who used to come and watch until a few years ago. Counted the steps up to the shrine every time he left." Grandpa.
You fold the cloth over it again. For a second it smells like Grandpa's house: incense, rice, rain.

events.title: Gotoda-senpai's letter
events.text: Gotoda-senpai corners you behind the budokan, red to the ears. "The kyudo captain. Sakaki-senpai. I want to ask her to the Tanabata festival. You're quiet. Quiet people know words. Help me."

choices.say: Three drafts. The third one is just: 'Will you come to the festival with me? - Gotoda.' He reads it aloud and goes pale. "It's perfect. I hate it." He sends it anyway.
"To her FACE?" He stares at you like you've suggested seppuku. Then he squares his shoulders and marches off. From the archery range: a very long silence, then a laugh. A yes-sounding laugh.
"...You're right. Kendo first." He lasts nine minutes before he asks you again.

events.title: Night practice
events.text: You come back for your forgotten bag. The budokan lights are off, but someone is practising in the dark: the slap of bare feet, a shinai cutting air. In the moonlight, an old set of armour moves on its own. The name tag inside it read ASAGIRI G.

choices.t: Pick up a shinai and bow.
choices.say: The armour bows back. One exchange: it is slow, and kind, and leaves you an opening so wide a child could find it. You take it. The armour sits down against the wall and is just armour again.

choices.t: Use the opening you once found against Gotoda-senpai.
choices.say: You wait, like you did that first day. The armour waits too - and then, impossibly, it laughs: a dry old man's laugh you haven't heard since the funeral. It falls still. On the floor, written in dust: GOOD BOY.

The shinai lowers. The helmet turns to look at the door, at the steps beyond it, and then it is empty. Mio, when you tell her, says objects loved long enough grow a little soul. "Not a hundred years. Just loved enough."

events.title: The last tournament of the term
events.text: Regional round, a sports hall in the city. Lacquered armour, a thousand voices, a scoreboard that has never once had Suzunari Gakuen on it after lunch.

choices.say: Gotoda-senpai lets you walk first, because you got them here. You lose in the quarter-final by one point. The club cries on the bus. Gotoda-senpai cries the most. It is the best day the club has had in nine years.
You win one bout and lose one. Gotoda-senpai shakes your helmet with both hands. "Next year. NEXT YEAR."
You cheer until you lose your voice. Afterwards Gotoda-senpai buys everyone ramen and makes you give a speech in a whisper.

track.name: Track Club
track.pitch: Hayate jogs over, grinning. "You're joining. Don't argue. Mon to Thu, we run till the sun gives up. I'll make you fast, Asagiri."
track.amane: "Inukai-senpai's club. ...Of course it is. I'll watch from the fence. Just watching."
track.amane_day: Amane watched every lap from behind the fence. When Hayate waved at him, he hid behind a cherry tree too thin to hide behind.
sessions: Interval sprints on the cinder track. Hayate runs the last one with you, a step behind, on purpose.
Hill repeats up the road to the shrine. At the top Hayate always looks east, toward Inukai Shrine, for exactly one breath.
Baton practice. Hayate's hand is warm and steady; yours keeps fumbling until it doesn't.

events.title: Relay trials
events.text: "Four places on the relay team," says Hayate. "Three are taken. Race me for the last one?"

choices.say: You lose by a body length, and he looks happier than if you'd won. "You're on the team. Anchor leg is mine; second leg is yours."
"Don't you dare," Hayate says, and makes you run it again. You're on the team anyway.

events.title: Hayate's personal best
events.text: Dusk. Hayate's stopwatch reads 11.02. He stares at it. "My mum ran 11.0 at my age. Inukai women run fast and die young, Grandpa says."

choices.say: "Yeah?" He looks at you for a long second. "Yeah." He runs another, and another, until it's dark.
He laughs, too loud. "Promise?" You say yes. Somewhere in the ledger a brush moves.

events.title: Rain practice
events.text: It's pouring. Amane must be crying somewhere. Hayate is already running laps.

choices.say: Mud to the knees. You both laugh like idiots. At the fence, an umbrella twitches.
He's under the gym eaves, sleeves over his hands, red-eyed. You sit with him. The rain thins to a drizzle.

events.title: The night before the sports festival
events.text: 21:00. The schoolyard floodlights are off, but somebody is running laps in the dark. Hayate. He is limping, and pretending he isn't.

choices.say: He sits on the kerb and lets you, scowling at the sky. "Don't tell Dad." Then, quieter: "You're good at this. Looking after people. Who taught you?" Nobody did.
"Dogs don't rest before a race." But he stops. He walks you to the gate with his hands in his pockets and his limp almost gone.

choices.t: Run a slow lap with him.
choices.say: One lap, in the dark, at an old man's pace. He laughs halfway round, a real one. "You're the worst pacer ever. Do it again."

events.title: Something follows you home
events.text: After evening practice the road along the hill is dark. Footsteps behind you, soft, padded, keeping exactly your pace. A white dog, the size of a calf, walking where your shadow should be.

choices.say: You don't run and you don't trip. At your door you turn and say, "Thank you for walking me home." The dog sits, satisfied, and is gone. That's how it works with okuri-inu: thank them, and they were only ever a bodyguard.
You run. You don't trip - just. The dog runs beside you all the way, tongue out, enjoying itself enormously. At the door it huffs, almost a laugh, and vanishes.

choices.t: Tell Hayate about it next day.
choices.say: Hayate goes very still. "A white dog. Big. Walked you home." He looks away. "...Good. That's - good. Lots of dogs around here." His ears, if he had dog's ears, would be down.

events.title: Eleven seconds
events.text: The last practice before the summer break. Hayate's best is still 11.02. "One more time," he says. "Clock me. Or run me. Whatever makes me faster."

choices.say: You run the first sixty metres beside him and then you are behind him, which is the point. The stopwatch reads 10.98. He doesn't celebrate. He sits down on the track and covers his face, and you sit next to him until he's done.
You lose by a body length, and he still runs 11.01 because you were close enough to scare him. "Again," he says, delighted. "Every day. Until you beat me."
10.99. He makes you show him three times. "My mum's going to say it was the wind." He's grinning so hard it looks painful.

music.name: Light Music & Choir
music.pitch: The music room smells of rosin and old sheet music. A second-year with a bass guitar shrugs: "Tue and Thu. We need anyone who can hold a note. Or a tambourine."
music.amane: "Senpai will sing? ...I-I'll record it. For research."
music.amane_day: Afterwards Amane hums the song you practised, slightly wrong, all the way to the gate.
sessions: Scales, scales, harmonies, scales. The upright piano is a semitone flat and nobody has the heart to fix it.
The choir practises a song for the Tanabata festival about two stars and a river. Everyone sings it a little too sadly.
You tune guitars while the drummer argues with the metronome. The metronome wins.

events.title: The piano by the window
events.text: Everyone has gone. The lid of the old upright is open. The keys are yellow, like teeth.

choices.t: Play the lullaby your hands remember.
choices.say: Your hands find a lullaby you never learned. From the corridor comes a sound like someone trying very hard not to cry.
Chopsticks, badly, at double speed. Somebody in the corridor laughs - a small, surprised laugh.
Dust puffs up. You close the window too. Some doors are easier shut.

events.title: Spring concert
events.text: The gym, folding chairs, three hundred parents. You're on after the brass band.

choices.say: Your voice cracks once and nobody cares. In the back row, a hood. Two ears, flat with joy.
Nobody remembers your song. That's fine. You remember the applause anyway.

events.title: Toryanse
events.text: 18:00. The town chime should be playing Toryanse from the pole outside. Instead, the old upright by the window plays it, lid up, nobody at the keys. Going in is easy. Coming back is frightening.

choices.say: Your fingers find it without being taught. The piano stops, as if satisfied, exactly as the town chime starts outside. The second-years look at you very carefully for the rest of the week.
The music stops under your hands like a held breath let go. Mizuno-senpai, on bass, says nothing. Then: "It does that in June. Thanks for being polite to it."
Your voice is better than you thought. Somewhere outside, under the window, someone in a black hood is singing the harmony.

events.title: A song for the festival
events.text: The choir has been asked to sing on the shrine stage at Tanabata. Mizuno-senpai wants your opinion. "Pick the song. You've got the face of someone who knows songs."

choices.say: "Creepy. Perfect." The choir practises it until it stops being creepy and becomes something sad and kind.
The first-years cheer. Mizuno-senpai sighs and teaches the bass line with the air of a martyr.

choices.t: Hum the lullaby Aunt Haruka sang.
choices.say: You hum it, and the room goes quiet. "Where's that from?" asks Mizuno-senpai. You don't know. It's from before you. The choir learns it in a day, as if they already half knew it.

events.title: The tambourine
events.text: Amane is in the doorway of the music room, holding a tambourine like a shield. "I can - I can keep time. I'm very good at waiting for the right moment. Ask anyone."

choices.say: The second-years shrug and make room. He is, it turns out, very good at waiting for the right moment. For an hour he forgets to look at you, and plays.
"Hayase-senpai...?" He looks at the tambourine, then at you, as if you have handed him a map. "Okay. I'll ask her. I'll ask her myself."
He sits next to you for the whole practice, tambourine silent on his knees, perfectly happy and completely useless.

events.title: Concert night
events.text: Tanabata eve, the shrine stage, lanterns, the whole town in yukata. The choir files on. You have the solo at the start.

choices.say: Your voice carries down the 999 steps. Afterwards a grandmother you've never met grips your hands and won't let go. "You sound just like him," she says, and leaves before you can ask who.
You sing to the dark at the bottom of the stairs instead of the people. Something down there is listening. When you finish, every lantern on the steps flickers once, together.

choices.t: Give the solo to a first-year.
choices.say: She is terrified and wonderful. You stand in the back row and nobody notices you at all, which is exactly what you wanted, once.

cooking.name: Cooking Club
cooking.prompt: Cooking Club (science lab, the Bunsen burners)
cooking.pitch: Home ec shares the science lab. A first-year in a frilly apron waves a ladle: "Wed and Fri! We cook, we eat, we wash up! Mostly we eat!"
cooking.amane: "Senpai's cooking... Who eats it? Who gets to eat it? ...Can it be me?"
cooking.amane_day: Amane is waiting at the door with an empty bento box and an expression of enormous hope.
sessions: Tamagoyaki practice. The trick is the flick of the wrist; the trick is also not setting the lab on fire.
Onigiri, three hundred of them, for the track team. Your palms smell of salt and seaweed for hours.
Curry rice over a Bunsen burner. The science teacher looks the other way for a spoonful.

events.title: Something for Amane
events.text: Leftover rice, two eggs, a sausage. Enough for one bento.

choices.say: He holds it in both hands like a kitten. "I can't eat it. It's too... I'm keeping it." He eats it eleven seconds later, crying.
Hayate inhales it. Behind the door, someone's shadow goes very still.
It's good. You're good at this. It's strange to be good at something.

events.title: Bento contest
events.text: The club's monthly contest. Judges: the principal, the school nurse, and a stray cat who wandered in.

choices.say: The cat eats the whole thing before the principal gets a bite. You win on the cat's vote.
Matcha curry. The principal says 'interesting' four times. The cat leaves.

events.title: Inari for the foxes
events.text: Kawai Momo, the first-year in the frilly apron, is making inarizushi. Outside the sun is shining and it's raining at the same time. "A fox wedding!" she says. "Leave some on the windowsill. They'll be hungry after."

choices.say: In the morning the plate is clean and there's a single wet ginkgo leaf on it, folded like a thank-you card. Momo is unbearable about it for a week.
Momo looks at you with deep pity. The sunshower stops the moment you say it, as if someone heard and was offended.
They're very good. Momo says you'll have bad luck for a week. You don't. But you trip over the same nothing, in the same place, every day for a week.

events.title: Chiyo-san's nikujaga
events.text: Chiyo-san comes into the lab to borrow the big pot and stays to teach. "Amane eats this when he's sad. Which is always. Peel the potatoes thinner, child."

choices.say: You bring it to him in a jar. He eats it on the school roof without a word, then cries a little, then laughs at himself for crying. "It tastes like Grandma's. But it's yours."
Her hands stop on the potato. "Sayo made it too sweet. Every time. I never told her." She starts peeling again. "Don't make my mistakes, child. Tell people things."
Haruka eats two bowls standing up in the shop and tells you it's terrible and asks for the recipe.

events.title: Rainy season
events.text: June. Everything in the lab is damp. The rice has a smell. The sugar has become one sugar. Momo is close to tears. The monthly contest is tomorrow.

choices.t: Make onigiri with the good rice.
choices.say: You find one dry bag at the back of the cupboard. Simple onigiri, perfect salt. The judges - the principal, the nurse and the stray cat - are unanimous.

choices.t: Turn the brick of sugar into dango syrup.
choices.say: Mitarashi dango, glossy and slightly burnt. The cat judge licks the plate and leaves you a dead cicada as a tribute.
The club plays cards instead and eats biscuits. Nobody wins the contest. Everyone is happy. Somewhere it stops raining for an hour.

events.title: The last bento
events.text: The day before Tanabata, the club makes one bento each for someone who matters. Momo is making hers for the stray cat. You have exactly enough rice for one.

choices.say: Rice shaped like a cat, eggs like a bell. He holds the box like it might break and doesn't eat it for an hour, just looks at it.
He eats it in four bites standing up and then thanks you so loudly the whole schoolyard hears. A black hood at the fence turns away.
You eat it on the roof alone, slowly, and it's good, and nobody is waiting for you to finish. It's strange how rare that has been.

occult.name: Occult Research Club
occult.pitch: Mio sits on a vaulting box surrounded by candles that are definitely against the rules. "Membership: one. Me. Tue and Fri until the ghosts get bored. You'd make it two. Do you see ghosts? Don't answer. I can tell."
occult.amane: "Kuroe-senpai's club... She looks at me like she knows. Senpai, don't tell her about my ears."
occult.amane_day: Mio watched Amane through the storeroom window the whole time. Amane watched her back. Nobody blinked.
sessions: Mio reads you the school's seven mysteries from a notebook bound in a cat-print cover. You take notes. She corrects your spelling of 'kamikakushi'.
Night camera tests on the third-floor corridor. Every photo has one extra shadow. Mio is delighted.
Mio teaches you the old way to count the 999 steps without the 13th one counting you back.

events.title: Kokkuri-san
events.text: A ten-yen coin on a sheet of paper with the kana, a torii and YES/NO. "Fingers on the coin," says Mio. "If it asks to stay, we say no. Always."

choices.say: The coin slides: N-E-K-O. Then: M-I-N-E. Then the window rattles and Mio says, very fast, "Kokkuri-san, please go home." It does. Mostly.
The coin moves to the torii and stops. It won't move again. Mio looks at you strangely. "It went home on its own. They never do that."

choices.t: Take your finger off the coin.
choices.say: "Coward," says Mio, approvingly. "Cowards live longest in this club."

events.title: The survey
events.text: Mio wants an interview with Hanako of the third-floor girls' toilet. For the club bulletin. Somebody has to knock three times.

choices.say: Knock, knock, knock. 'Hanako-san, shall we play?' A small voice: 'Not today. Tell Mio her bulletin has a typo.' It does.
She does, without hesitation. Nothing answers her. She sulks for the rest of the hour.

events.title: The thirteenth step
events.text: Mio has a clipboard. "Mystery four: the west staircase has twelve steps by day and thirteen after six. We count it together. If it's thirteen, we don't step on the last one."

choices.say: Twelve. Thirteen. You both stop on the twelfth. The thirteenth is slightly darker than the others, and warm, like something has been sitting on it. Mio writes 'CONFIRMED' and underlines it three times.

The staircase lurches. You're on the landing of a floor that doesn't exist - long, red-lit, a corridor full of empty desks - and then Mio has your collar and you're back. "Idiot," she says, shaking. "Idiot. Don't do that."
She gets thirteen. Then twelve. Then she refuses to count again and you go and get melon bread instead.

events.title: Salt
events.text: Mio's grandmother, Kuroe Setsu, comes to collect her. She looks at you, then at the air just behind your shoulder, and takes a pinch of salt from her sleeve.

choices.say: Salt on both shoulders. Something you didn't know you were carrying gets lighter. "Cats follow you," says Setsu. "One of them is not a cat. Be kind to it anyway."
"A boy who is also a cat who is also waiting." She pockets the salt. "Not a bad thing to have behind you. Just a heavy one."
"Polite," says Setsu, "but salt finds its way." It lands on your shoe. Mio is trying very hard not to laugh.

events.title: Mapping the parade
events.text: Mio unrolls a map of Suzunari on the floor and weighs it down with jizo figurines. "The night parade of a hundred demons comes down the steps before Tanabata. I want the route. For safety. And for the bulletin."

choices.say: You trace the oldest streets, the ones that curve for no reason. Mio nods slowly. "They curve around something that was there before the houses." She shivers, delighted.
Every cat spot you know. The route draws itself: walls, the station, the bridge, the steps. Mio stares. "They're not sitting. They're keeping the road."

choices.t: "What if we just stay home that night?"
choices.say: "Sensible," says Mio. "Boring. I'll go alone and bring you a photo." You know she will.

events.title: The club photo
events.text: End of term. Mio sets her old camera on a timer for the first ever Occult Research Club photo: two members, one vaulting box, too many candles. The film comes back from the shop a week later.

choices.say: Two members and a third: a small girl with a gold bell at her throat, standing between you, looking straight at the lens. Mio puts the photo in a plastic sleeve and doesn't say anything for a long time. "She was in the 2016 photo too," she says at last.
"Never." Mio hugs the photo to her chest. "This is the best thing the club has ever done." She makes you a copy anyway. You keep it in a book you don't open.
She holds them side by side over the lamp: two photos, ten years apart, the same girl with the same bell. Mio's hands are steady. Her voice isn't. "Asagiri. Who is she?"

newspaper.name: Newspaper Club
newspaper.pitch: Hina spins in her chair, pen behind her ear. "Mon and Thu we make the Suzunari Shimbun. Facts only. Mostly facts. You'd be good at it - nobody notices you, so everybody talks in front of you."
newspaper.amane: "Hayase-senpai asks a lot of questions. About me. Please don't answer them, Senpai."
newspaper.amane_day: This week's Suzunari Shimbun has a blurry photo of a black cat with two tails. The caption says 'PHOTO: ANONYMOUS'. It was you.
sessions: Proofreading. Hina writes like she talks: fast, with too many exclamation marks. You delete forty-one of them.
Layout on an ancient laptop. The club's only printer jams on every page with a cat on it.
Door-to-door interviews about the rain. Everyone says the same thing: it rains when a certain first-year is sad.

events.title: The Ura board story
events.text: Hina wants to expose the school's anonymous board. "Someone posts the rival's name every Monday. Who?"

choices.say: Three late nights later Hina has a theory and no proof. She looks at Amane's class photo for a long time.
"Some stories eat the reporter," you say. She stares at you. "...That's a good line. I'm stealing it." She drops the story.

events.title: Interview the president
events.text: Hina needs a quote from Shirasagi Reiji about the festival budget. He doesn't give quotes.

choices.say: Reiji looks at you a long moment. "Write that the council will hold the festival rain or shine." Then, quieter: "Off the record: especially rain."
Hina prints it. Reiji reads it, and for one second looks almost amused.

events.title: The weather column
events.text: Hina has a chart on the wall: rain in Suzunari against attendance in 1-A. One absent first-year matches every storm. "Nekomori Amane," she says. "Weather forecast: him. I want to run it."

choices.t: "Run the weather. Leave his name out."
choices.say: She chews her pen for a whole minute. "Fine. Sources protected." The forecast becomes the most popular column in the paper. Nobody knows why it's always right.
You tell her about the tears and the rain. She doesn't laugh. She closes the notebook. "Then that's not a story," she says. "That's a person." She takes the chart down herself.
"Nothing is a coincidence in this town." But she leaves it, for now. You see her watching the sky afterwards, then the first-year windows.

events.title: The maneki-neko factory
events.text: Golden Week special: a tour of the Shirasagi maneki-neko factory. Ten thousand lucky cats on a conveyor belt, all waving. In the yard, the giant one with the cracked paw.

choices.say: The guide's smile freezes. "It cracked in 2010. The year the shrine went quiet. Coincidence." Hina writes COINCIDENCE in capital letters and circles it.
Left paws bring people, right paws bring money. Every cat on the line waves its right paw. Hina is impressed despite herself. "A town that only wants money. That's the headline."

choices.t: Photograph Reiji in the office window.
choices.say: He's standing behind his mother, very still. When he sees the camera he doesn't hide. He just looks at it. Hina decides not to print it.

events.title: A letter to the editor
events.text: An envelope in the club postbox, no stamp, smelling of rain: 'Please stop writing about the cat. He is trying his best. - A reader'. The handwriting is very small and very careful.

choices.say: Hina holds it up to the window. "Then he's braver than I thought." She pins it to the wall where the chart used to be and never writes about the cat again.
It runs on page two. The next day Amane walks past the club room three times, very fast, very red, and on the fourth time he puts a thank-you note under the door.
'Dear reader: he is. - The editors.' Hina lets you have the last word. It's the shortest article the Suzunari Shimbun has ever run.

events.title: The last issue of term
events.text: One front page left before summer. Hina spreads out the candidates: a Tanabata festival guide, a blurry photo of a lantern on the hill on the 13th night, and a picture of you she took without asking.

choices.say: Maps, stalls, the best place to watch the lanterns. Practical, kind, boring. Every copy is gone by lunch.
"Who lights a lantern on the hill every 13th?" The Shirasagi family's lawyer calls the school that afternoon. Hina frames the letter.

choices.t: Run the follow-up to her big story.
choices.say: Part two. She was right to publish, and now she has the names to prove it. The Suzunari Shimbun sells out to adults for the first time in its history.

council.name: Student Council
council.pitch: Shirasagi Reiji doesn't look up from the budget. "Tue and Fri. Paperwork, the festival, the rules. You'd be useful. People don't notice you - they say things in front of you."
council.amane: "The council... Shirasagi-senpai's family owns half the town. Be careful, Senpai. They own people too."
council.amane_day: Amane slipped a note under the council door: 'PLEASE RETURN SENPAI BY 18:00.'
sessions: Stamping forms. A thousand of them. Reiji stamps faster than you thought humanly possible.
The festival committee argues about lanterns. Reiji ends it with one sentence and a look.
Filing complaints about the rain. Seventeen this week. Reiji files them under 'weather' without comment.

events.title: The budget meeting
events.text: The occult club's budget is zero. The kendo club wants a new floor. There's money for one.

choices.t: Give it to the occult club.
choices.say: Reiji raises an eyebrow and signs. Somewhere on the third floor, a delighted shriek.
The budokan gets its floor. The squeaky board that hums is replaced. Some nights, the new one hums too.
"Fair," says Reiji, "and useless." He sounds like he's quoting someone.

events.title: His father's call
events.text: Reiji's phone buzzes: FATHER. He lets it ring. Then, to you: "If you had a name that owned a town, would you want it?"

choices.say: "Yes," he says. "I thought you would." He answers the phone. His voice changes completely.
He's quiet. "...That's the answer my grandfather gave. Before he lost the shrine."

events.title: The lantern order
events.text: Three hundred paper lanterns for the Tanabata steps. Two suppliers: the old Kuroe workshop by the temple, or Shirasagi Trading, at half the price.

choices.say: Reiji signs it without comment. That evening his phone rings: MOTHER. He lets it ring. "Good choice," he says, to the budget sheet.
The lanterns arrive in a week, perfect and identical, each stamped with a tiny white heron. Reiji looks at the stamp for a long time.

choices.t: Ask the club kids to make them.
choices.say: Two hundred lanterns, folded by every club in the school, wonky and wonderful. The council room is buried in paper for a fortnight. Reiji almost smiles.

events.title: A petition about cats
events.text: A petition from the PTA: remove the stray cats from school grounds, "for hygiene". Forty signatures. The first one is S. Kyoko.

choices.say: You argue for twenty minutes. Reiji lets you. Then he stamps it REJECTED in red. "For the record," he says, "I agree with you. For the record, I wasn't here."
Clean bowls by the gym, a rota, the cats fed in one place. Even the PTA can't object to a rota. A week later the cats sit in a neat row watching the council room window.
Reiji looks at your name next to his mother's. He doesn't say anything. That night something scratches your window for an hour.

events.title: The speech
events.text: Reiji has to give the opening speech at the festival. He hands you the draft. The handwriting is perfect. The speech is perfect. It doesn't sound like anyone.

choices.say: He stares at you. Then he takes the pen. The new speech is half a page long and mentions the harbour once. His hand shakes on the last line. He doesn't cross it out.

choices.t: Fix the grammar and leave it.
choices.say: "Thank you." He means it. He also folds the speech into a very small square, as if he wants it to be smaller.
"Choose?" The word sits on his desk like a stone. He writes it at the top of the page and nothing else, for a long time.

events.title: Tanabata wishes
events.text: The council collects the tanzaku from the wish bamboo before the festival. You sort them. Most want good grades. One says, in very small writing: 'I want Senpai to remember.' One, in perfect handwriting: 'I want to choose.'

choices.t: Hang them both at the top.
choices.say: Highest branch, side by side. Reiji sees, and says nothing, and stays late to straighten them in the wind.
You write it quickly, before you can think. You don't let anyone see it. The paper is warm when you tie it on, like a hand.

choices.t: Read the rest aloud to Reiji.
choices.say: 'Pass the exam.' 'Pass the exam.' 'A girlfriend.' 'For Grandma's knee to get better.' He listens to every one. "These are the people we work for," he says, as if he's only just found out.

go_home.name: Go-Home Club
go_home.prompt: Go-Home Club (walk home the long way)
go_home.pitch: There is no room, no captain and no flyer, just a line in pencil at the bottom of the board: GO-HOME CLUB. Under it, very small, one name already: Nekomori Amane (1-A).
go_home.amane: "S-Senpai joined the Go-Home Club? Then... then it has two members. I'm the president. I just decided."
go_home.amane_day: The Go-Home Club walked home by the river. The president held the treasurer's sleeve the whole way.
sessions: You walk home the long way, along the river. Nobody asks you where you're going. That's the whole club.
Club activity: buying a melon pan and eating it on the bridge. The president gets half.
You take the back streets and count the cats. Eleven. They all look at you like you owe them something.

events.title: The president's agenda
events.text: Amane has written an agenda. Item one: walk Senpai home. Item two: walk Senpai home again. Item three: (secret).

choices.say: He goes red to the ears. "It's... we hold hands at the bridge. Only if the treasurer agrees. The treasurer is you."
"...The club has rules." But he comes. He walks half a step behind and doesn't sulk until the gate.
"Oh." He stands at the gate as you go. When you look back, he waves, and he's smiling, a little. That's new.

events.title: The long way
events.text: The president has decided the club walks home by the river today. Halfway along he stops at a bench under a cherry tree. "A white-and-black cat used to sit here," he says. "Every evening. For years. Waiting for a boy."

choices.say: "It got old." He sits on the bench, where the cat sat. "And then it got born again, and it's still waiting, and it's very embarrassing, Senpai, please stop looking at me."

choices.t: Sit on the bench with him.
choices.say: You sit. The river goes past. A cat comes and sits on the other end of the bench, the way cats do. Nobody says anything for ten minutes. It's the best club meeting so far.
"...Right. Yes. Onwards." He walks a little faster after that, but he doesn't look back at the bench, which is new.

events.title: One umbrella
events.text: Halfway home it starts to rain - real rain, from nowhere, the way it does here. The club has one umbrella between two members.

choices.say: He holds it, because he insists, and it covers you completely and him not at all. You take it off him and hold it in the middle. He walks very carefully so that your shoulders don't touch. Then they do.
"But then Senpai gets wet." You get wet. He walks the whole way home under the umbrella looking stricken, and the rain stops the moment you reach your door.
He stops. The rain doesn't. "...Because I was happy," he says, very quietly, "and then I thought about the end of term." You stand there until it eases.

events.title: The treasurer's report
events.text: The club funds are 120 yen, found in a vending machine slot by the president. As treasurer, you must decide.

choices.say: He insists you have the first bite and then eats the rest at tremendous speed with his eyes shut. "Club budget well spent," he announces.
"A responsible treasurer." He writes '120 yen (saved)' in his notebook in very neat handwriting, and seems happier about it than about any ice.

choices.t: Give it to the jizo by the crossroads.
choices.say: You put the coins in front of the little stone figure. Amane bows to it, solemn. "For the children who don't get to walk home," he says. You don't ask how he knows to say that.

events.title: A new member
events.text: The president has a crisis. Kuroe-senpai wants to join the Go-Home Club. "For research." Hayase-senpai wants to join too. "For the paper." The club has never had three members.

choices.say: "Th-then it's four." He stares at the number on his agenda. Then he writes the names under his own, slowly, in his best handwriting. The walk home is loud and chaotic and he laughs twice.
He thinks about it all the way to the bridge. "...One meeting a week can be just us," he decides. "The rest can be everyone." He seems surprised by himself.
He glows. Then, at the gate, he looks back at the two girls walking away and his face does something complicated.

events.title: The last walk before Tanabata
events.text: July. The last club walk before the festival. At the foot of the 999 steps the president stops and doesn't go on. "Senpai. On the seventh. Will you come to the steps?"

choices.say: He doesn't jump or cry. He just nods, once, as if a very old question has been answered. "Then I'll wait. I'm good at that part."
"Alone?" He looks up the steps, then back at you. "...Okay. I'll bring Kuroe-senpai. And a lantern. And snacks." It's the most normal plan he's ever made.
"That's okay." It isn't, quite. A drop of rain lands on the step between you. "Not knowing is better than no," he says, and means it, and walks home on his own.

konbini.name: Suzunari Mart (night shift)
konbini.interview: The night manager has a long, elegant neck and a name tag: YAMANE. "Night shift. 18:30 to 21:30, Mon, Wed, Fri, Sat. ¥1,050 an hour. Don't stare at anything that stretches, and you'll be fine."
konbini.hired: "Wonderful. Wear the vest. Never restock the top shelf - that's my job."
work: Restocking onigiri, ringing up instant noodles, smiling at drunk salarymen. The fluorescent lights hum the Tanabata song.
Three customers in three hours: a salaryman with no face (he buys coffee), a fox in a schoolgirl's coat (inari sushi), and a cat (it just stares at the fish).
You mop the floor twice. The second time, there are wet paw prints from the door to the cat food aisle and back.

events.title: The top shelf
events.text: A customer needs the last box of senbei on the top shelf. You turn round to fetch the stepladder. Behind you, Yamane-san's head is already up there, on a neck three metres long.

choices.say: "Here you are," she says, at normal height again, handing it over. She gives you a tiny nod. Pretending is a kindness, here.
Her neck goes pink, all three metres of it. "Nobody's ever thanked me for that." You get an extra ¥500 in your envelope.
Both of you scream. The customer screams. The cat screams. Then everyone laughs, a bit hysterically.

events.title: A boy outside the window
events.text: 21:00. A hooded figure has been standing outside the glass for half an hour, umbrella up, in no rain at all.

choices.t: Bring him a hot can of cocoa.
choices.say: He takes it in both sleeves. "I wasn't waiting. I was... passing. For thirty minutes." He walks you home.
He waves back, a tiny flap of sleeve. He stays till closing.

choices.t: Ask Yamane-san to send him home.
choices.say: Yamane-san goes outside. You don't hear what she says. He leaves, and the rain starts.

events.title: Yamane-san's neck
events.text: 21:10. Restocking. You turn round with a box of senbei and Yamane-san's head is level with the top shelf, smiling, and her body is still at the till.

choices.say: "Thank you," says the head, kindly, and comes back down. Your pay packet that week has an extra thousand yen in it and a note: FOR YOUR EYESIGHT.
"Only in winter." The neck folds itself away like a garden hose. "Nobody has ever asked me that." She gives you a meat bun and won't take money for it.
She looks at the stepladder, then at you, and laughs, a long laugh that goes up and up. She uses the stepladder.

events.title: The last customer
events.text: 21:29, one minute to closing. A man in a suit buys a bento, a can of coffee and a pair of disposable chopsticks. He has no face. Just smooth skin, like an egg.

choices.say: A long pause. "...Yes, please." The voice comes from nowhere in particular. He bows on the way out. Yamane-san, at the back, gives you a thumbs-up.
You scream. He screams too, from nowhere, and drops the coffee. You both apologise at the same time. He leaves with the bento and you mop up the coffee, shaking.
"I take the last bus," he says. "I've been taking it for a long time." He leaves a thousand yen and doesn't wait for change.

cat_cafe.name: Cat Cafe Nekonote
cat_cafe.interview: Tamaki-san, apron covered in fur, inspects you. Nine cats inspect you too. "Tue and Thu after school, Sunday late morning. The cats choose the staff. Let's see."
cat_cafe.hired: A tabby sits on your foot. "Hired," says Tamaki-san. "She never does that."
work: Latte art (a cat, badly). Customers take photos of the real cats and ignore the latte.
You brush seven cats. All the town's cats seem to know you worked here today; they're friendlier on the way home.
A regular who comes every day to sit with the oldest cat, Daifuku. Today she talks to you instead. About her late husband. Daifuku listens too.

events.title: Daifuku's last nap
events.text: Daifuku, the cafe's oldest cat, won't get up. Tamaki-san sits with him. "Twenty-two years. He's ready. Will you stay?"

choices.say: He goes in his sleep, purring, with the sun on him. Outside a two-tailed shadow sits on the fence and bows its head. You see it. It sees you seeing it.
Amane comes running. He kneels and says something to Daifuku in a language that isn't Japanese. Daifuku purrs once more. Amane cries for everyone.

events.title: A face at the window
events.text: Amane, pressed against the cafe window, watching you pet a white cat. His expression is complicated.

choices.say: Every cat in the cafe lines up in front of him and bows. Tamaki-san drops a tray. Amane tries to look innocent.
The white cat purrs. The window is empty. Your phone buzzes: 'she's very pretty. i'm not jealous of a CAT. ok bye.'

events.title: The cat committee
events.text: Closing time. You're wiping the tables when the cats climb onto the counter, one by one, and sit in a circle. The big ginger one clears his throat.

choices.say: "Item one: the boy with the bell is crying again. Item two: we report the girl from the flower shop." They see you. Eleven cats look at you. The ginger one says, very clearly, "Minutes not taken."
The meeting dissolves into chaos. When it's over, the ginger one rubs against your leg. You have, it seems, bribed the committee.

choices.t: Turn the lights off and go home.
choices.say: Behind you, in the dark: "Sensible," says a voice. Then, "Item three..."

events.title: A customer who only orders milk
events.text: A regular now: Amane, at the window table, a glass of warm milk, every Tuesday. He never orders anything else. He watches you work with his chin in his hands.

choices.t: Bring him milk with a heart in the foam.
choices.say: He stares at the heart until it disappears. Then he drinks the milk very slowly. He tips you a hundred yen, which is all he has.

choices.t: Sit with him on your break.
choices.say: Five minutes. A tabby climbs into his lap and he freezes, terrified and delighted. "They don't usually let me," he whispers. "They know what I am."
He tries the cake. He has a strong opinion about the cake. He has opinions about all the cakes, it turns out, and Tamaki-san hires him to taste them.

sweets.name: Asagiri-do (Aunt Haruka's sweet shop)
sweets.interview: Haruka hands you an apron before you've finished asking. "Wednesdays after school and weekend mornings. Family rate. Which means low."
sweets.hired: "Rule one: smile. Rule two: the dango on the left are for the jizo, not for you."
work: You make dango until your fingers are sticky to the wrist. Haruka sings enka off-key the whole time.
Old ladies buy warabi-mochi and tell you who you look like: your grandfather. Every single one.
A quiet afternoon. Haruka tells you about the summer you were six and fell asleep in the shop's display window.

events.title: Grandpa's recipe book
events.text: Under the counter: a recipe book in Grandpa's handwriting. The last page isn't a recipe. It's a list of dates, all in July.

choices.say: "Your grandfather closed the shop every seventh of July and climbed the steps." She doesn't look at you. "Every year. Even the last one."
1868. 1890. 1945. 2016. And a blank line at the bottom, already ruled.

events.title: A very small customer
events.text: A girl in an old-fashioned kimono puts a leaf on the counter and asks for one dango. The leaf turns into a coin when you look away.

choices.say: She bows and runs into the house through a wall. Haruka, not looking up: "That's Kiku. Give her the burnt ones, she likes them."
She pouts and leaves. All afternoon the shop's bell rings with nobody there.

events.title: Kiku sulks
events.text: The shop is cold all morning. Customers walk past. The bell over the door doesn't ring. Aunt Haruka says the zashiki-warashi is sulking. "You left the back room a mess. Kiku hates mess."

choices.say: You tidy it properly, corners and all. In the afternoon the bell over the door rings by itself, and six customers come in at once.

choices.t: Leave a dango on the back step.
choices.say: In the morning there's a small hand-print in the flour on the counter and the dango is gone. The shop is warm again.
The till drawer slams on your fingers. Aunt Haruka doesn't even look up. "She does."

events.title: Three hundred dango
events.text: The shrine has ordered three hundred dango for Tanabata. Chiyo-san brings Amane to help. He is very good at rolling dango and very bad at not eating them.

choices.say: Ten dango each, fastest wins. Amane wins, and gets flour on his nose, and doesn't know, and you don't tell him all afternoon.
Three folds, a pinch of salt, a wish. He learns it faster than you did. Haruka watches the two of you with an odd look and goes to the back room for a while.

choices.t: Let him and Haruka do it.
choices.say: You do the deliveries. When you come back they're laughing at something, flour everywhere, and Haruka is calling him 'the little cat' like she's known him for years.

fish_market.name: Suzunari Harbour fish market
fish_market.prompt: Harbour fish market: work a morning
fish_market.interview: Old Man Gen looks at your arms and laughs. "Weekends, from first light. Ice, crates, fish, more ice. ¥1,300 an hour. Don't feed the cats, they're unionised."
fish_market.turned_down: "Come back when you can lift a crate without crying. Eat more rice." (Stamina 30 needed.)
fish_market.hired: "Boots are by the door. They're wet. They're always wet."
work: Crates of mackerel, buckets of ice. By ten you can't feel your fingers, but you can feel the cats watching from the breakwater.
The auction: a man shouting numbers at a speed that should be impossible. You understand one in five. Gen says that's good for a beginner.
You gut sardines. The harbour cats form an orderly queue. Gen pretends not to see you slip them the heads.

events.title: The catch that talks
events.text: A fish in your crate opens its mouth and says, quite clearly: "Tell the boy with the bell the sea remembers 2011."

choices.t: Put it back in the sea.
choices.say: It flips once and is gone. On the horizon, for a moment, a dark shape the size of a hill watches the harbour.
Gen goes pale and pours sake into the sea. "Not every catch is ours to keep."

events.title: The cats are on strike
events.text: Dawn. Not a single cat on the harbour wall. The fishermen are worried. Old Man Gen is furious. "Somebody fed them. Now they want benefits."

choices.say: You crouch by a three-legged tom with a torn ear and offer one sardine a day. He considers. He accepts. By noon the harbour wall is full of cats again and Gen calls you 'the union rep'.
Gen glares. Then he laughs so hard he has to sit on a crate. "Honest boy. Rare. You can feed them on Sundays. Only Sundays."
Ice, crates, more ice. The cats come back on their own at dusk, as if nothing happened, and look at you as if you were the one who left.

events.title: Ladles at dawn
events.text: Fog on the water. A boat with no lights drifts in past the breakwater, and pale hands come over its side holding ladles. "Give us a ladle," voices say. "Give us a ladle."

choices.t: Hand them a ladle with a hole in it.
choices.say: Gen taught you this on your first day. They bail and bail, and the water runs out through the hole, and at sunrise the boat is gone. Gen claps you on the back without a word.
The boat fills with seawater, fast. Gen grabs the ladle back out of the air and snaps it over his knee. "NEVER whole. Never." He's white as the fog.
You put your hands together. The voices go quiet, one by one. The boat turns and goes back out into the fog, slowly, like it's been waiting a long time for someone to just say sorry.

events.title: The boat that didn't come back
events.text: Gen is mending a net on his own when everyone else has gone. His hands are slow today. On the harbour wall behind him there's a small memorial with fresh flowers.

choices.say: You work in silence for an hour. "My boy," he says at last, not looking up. "A storm, fifteen years ago. He'd have liked you." He ties off the last knot.
"For the ones the sea kept." He looks out at the water. "In 2011 the sea took a woman from the steps. Folk say she's not in the sea, though. Folk say a lot of things."
You leave a can of hot coffee beside him. He doesn't say anything, but on Saturday your crate is the lightest one.

shrine.name: Suzune Shrine helper
shrine.interview: Chiyo-san leans on her broom. "Sweeping, omikuji, the offering box. Wednesday afternoons and weekend middays. Amane helps too. ...Yes. That's why I'm asking you."
shrine.turned_down: "Not yet. Meet my grandson first. He's the one who'll be sweeping beside you."
shrine.hired: "Wear this." A white haori. Amane, beside her, has gone completely silent and very red.
work: Sweeping the plaza. Amane sweeps the same square metre as you, very slowly, so it takes longer.
Omikuji for tourists. Amane folds them; you tie the bad ones to the pine. Every bad fortune he folds, he reads first, and quietly swaps.
Topping up the lantern oil. The bell in the hall doesn't ring, but every time you pass it, Amane touches his choker.

events.title: A fortune for Senpai
events.text: Amane holds out an omikuji. "Draw one. Any one. ...Not that one. That one."

choices.say: DAI-KICHI. Great blessing. 'The person you wait for will come.' He'd folded it himself. You keep it anyway.
KYO. Bad luck. 'Beware of what follows you.' Amane snatches it, ties it to the pine, and doesn't speak for ten minutes.

events.title: Sweeping the 999
events.text: Chiyo-san sends you both to sweep the steps. Halfway down, Amane stops. "Senpai... do you count them too?"

choices.say: "So did someone else," he whispers. He doesn't say who. He doesn't need to.
"Yes," he says, relieved. "Very weird. Nobody normal does it." He counts under his breath all the way down.

events.title: Ema
events.text: Writing ema plaques for visitors who can't write. An old woman wants 'a good marriage for my granddaughter'. A boy wants 'Mum to come home'. Then Amane writes his own and hangs it on the back of the rack, where nobody looks.

choices.say: 'I want Senpai to have friends who aren't me. I want to want that.' The ink is smudged where it got wet.
You hang yours beside it without reading his. When you look back, he's standing very still in front of the rack, reading yours.
Some wishes are private. Chiyo-san sees you not look, and nods, and gives you the good broom.

events.title: Five-yen coins
events.text: Counting the offering box with Chiyo-san at dusk. Hundreds of five-yen coins. "Go-en," she says. "Five yen, and en, fate. People don't pray for money here. They pray for ties."

choices.say: "Every Tanabata, one five-yen coin, very early in the morning. Nine years now." She doesn't say who. She doesn't have to.

choices.t: Add a coin of your own.
choices.say: It clinks against the others. Chiyo-san bows to the shrine on your behalf. "For what?" "I don't know yet." "That's the best kind."
Her hands stop counting. "Sayo put a coin in every day of her life. Then she stopped coming." She starts counting again from one, though she was at forty.
